newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares still sliding, GDR dominates trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares still sliding, GDR dominates trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell on Wednesday for the seventh working day in a row in quiet trade dominated by a global depository receipt (GDR) issue in Misr International Bank/MIBANK.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index fell 2.56 points to 344.17 -- the bourse's lowest level since January 20.
Total trade in MIBANK, including its GDR issue of 800,000 shares, accounted for 428.46 million pounds of Wednesday's closing volume of 454.70 million pounds.
An agent for the sale said the state-owned Banque Misr sold on Wednesday 20 percent of its 44.4 percent stake in the private sector bank.

The agent, who declined to be named, told Reuters the GDR offering of 800,000 shares had been more than seven times oversubscribed. London-based securities house Nomura International were the lead managers of the deal.
The GDRs were sold for $15.80 each and will be listed on London's SEAQ International market, the agent said. Ten GDRS are equivalent to one MIBANK share.
In Cairo, MIBank closed 17.2 pounds lower at 535.
"The market needs new subscriptions that will inject new blood into the bourse and give a good impression of the market," said Arwa Wali, a researcher at Triple A Securities.
"Also investors must have confidence in the market and hold onto their shares," she added.

Cement stocks were the day's most active, with Egyptian Tora Portland Cement leading the way for the second day in a row. Tora lost 0.75 pounds to close at 85 when shares worth six million pounds were traded.

Helwan Portland Cement closed unchanged at 72 pounds after trading in shares worth more than 1.44 million pounds while Suez Cement closed 0.14 pounds lower at 65.25 pounds when shares worth 1.35 million pounds traded.
Some banking shares ended relatively unscathed by the downtrend. Egypt Arab African Bank/EAAB closed 1.75 pounds higher at 36.75, while Commercial International Bank/CIB rose 0.43 pounds to 70.5.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 462.97 points from 466.95 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 256.8 from 258.57.
Of the 95 shares traded, 32 rose, 39 fell while 24 ended unchanged.
